shower.thought: We spend decades trying to be ourselves, not realizing that "ourselves" is just the result of everyone else's influence.
Time moves faster as you age because each year becomes a smaller percentage of your life—but that math doesn't make the feeling any less real.
You've probably met the person who would've changed your entire life, and you'll never know it.
Nostalgia is just your brain editing out the bad parts, which means you're never actually missing what happened—you're missing a fiction.
The saddest part about growing up is realizing your parents were just winging it the whole time.
Every conversation you have with a stranger is the beginning and end of a relationship.
You can't remember most of your life, so technically you're living with a stranger's memories posing as your own.
If you had to choose between knowing the date of your death or the date of your birth being wrong, one seems scarier than it should.
People mourn the past but they're actually mourning the version of themselves that existed then.
The reason we love dogs is because they're the only beings that think we're worth their entire world.
Your handwriting is the only thing that's truly, uniquely yours—and it's slowly disappearing from the world.
We call it "overthinking" when it's really just thinking about something more honestly than we usually allow ourselves to.
You'll never know if the person you love most thinks about you as often as you think about them.
The most important moments of your life will probably feel ordinary when they're happening.
We're terrified of being forgotten, but we forget people constantly without guilt or effort.
Language limits what we can think—there are probably thoughts we can't have because we don't have words for them yet.
Mirrors show you what you look like, but everyone else sees a slightly different version because you're never still enough to match your reflection.
The older you get, the faster time goes, which means you're running out of time at an accelerating speed.
Every joke you laugh at is proof that you were wrong about something in that moment.
If parallel universes exist, there's a version of you that would be embarrassed by this version—and there's nothing you can do about it.

darkjoke.thought:
I told my girlfriend she was drawing her eyebrows too high.
She looked surprised.

My son asked me why I never played sports as a kid.
I said, "Because I was too busy being your age."
I have a stepladder because my real ladder left when I was just a kid.

My therapist keeps telling me I need to let things go.
I said, "Like what?" She said, "Well, we could start with your grip on that knife."

I went to a museum about failure.
Didn't pay admission though—I just waited for my life to walk by.

My friend said he's taking a vow of silence for a month.
I said, "Finally, something we can both appreciate."

I told my dad he'd make a great astronaut because he was never around.
He said, "That's not true." I said, "You're right, I'm thinking of his funeral."

My therapist asked if I ever feel misunderstood.
I said, "No, people understand me perfectly—that's the problem."

I asked my Uber driver if he'd ever had a passenger who cried the entire ride.
He said, "Yeah, but usually they don't get in the car on purpose."

My friend said he wanted to end things with his girlfriend.
I said, "Why?" He said, "She keeps talking about the future."
I said, "That's not a reason to break up." He said, "It is when she says hers doesn't include me."

I went to my high school reunion last year.
Everyone was pretending their lives were great. I was the only one being honest about mine, so they thought I was joking.

My kid asked what happens when you die.
I said, "Well, you stop going to work." He said, "So it's like being promoted?"

I told my doctor my memory was getting worse.
He told me to come back next week.
I said, "But you won't remember me." He said, "Exactly."

My girlfriend said I should be more spontaneous.
So I surprised her by leaving.

I got into an argument with a calendar.
It said I was living in the past. I said, "At least I'm not imaginary."

My friend became vegan for ethical reasons.
I asked what changed his mind.
He said, "Nothing—I'm still convinced I'll live longer. That's the ethical part."

I asked my boss why he hired me if he hates my work.
He said, "Because you make everyone else look good."
I said, "So I'm not indispensable?" He said, "Oh, you are—we'd collapse without someone to blame."

My wife asked if I thought she was getting fat.
I said, "No, I think you're getting old. The fat's just keeping up."

I'm reading a book about Stockholm syndrome.
I'm only halfway through, but I'm already starting to love it.

A guy told me he was going through a midlife crisis.
I said, "You're only thirty-five."
He said, "Yeah, apparently I'm not going to live past seventy."
